F1 overstated the counting supplier by adding a saddle-sector classification. It now states only c_K−s_K=1. Step 1.1 applies it to the explicitly given simple one-quadrant inner disk; invariant boundary trajectories keep the search inside K, and a new interior frontier saddle is excluded from K′, giving strict saddle-count descent.

F2 and step 3.1 overclaimed arbitrary compact-band persistence and fixed filling-disk transport. The repair constructs the local prescribed C² trace in regular submersion strips and applies the supplier only near the base parameter. That interval contains both sides and suffices for the unchanged sufficiently-close-loop conclusion.

Step 2.1 inferred nonidentity from a frontier theorem supplying no such conclusion. The repaired return-strip graph bounds a smaller positively invariant transverse-boundary disk; applying the nonidentity-cycle selection theorem to that restricted separated generic disk supplies a genuinely nonidentity cycle, contradicting original inclusion-minimality. The three-sector case uses the selection theorem’s area minimum and the dedicated inward-identity supplier directly.

The exclusion of nontrivial holonomy was incorrectly two-sided: a vanishing Reeb boundary meridian may have nonidentity holonomy on the opposite side. The Definition now derives identity only on the approached half-transversal from closure of the whole loop family and explicitly leaves the opposite side unrestricted; conditions (i)–(iv) and the Π-class conclusion are preserved.

F3 incorrectly globalized connected spherical stability to disconnected M. The proof now restricts to the closed connected component M₀ containing L and W. A spherical boundary would foliate that component by spheres; their saturated product charts give a circle leaf space and a positive return through L, contradicting its no-transversal hypothesis. The finite Euler sum then forces every boundary genus to be one.

F1 overattributed base-gluing data to cap development. The repair distinguishes the supplied regular development from the explicitly assumed h and base equalities. Those actual hypotheses give plaque inverse branches with transverse half-neighbourhoods on opposite sides; compactness then yields the unchanged image-boundary containment without any new existence assertion.

Step 1.1 used an already-compact-leaf theorem to assert compact existence from common holonomy fixed points. It now constructs the graph using finite polygon transports and finitely many overlap homotopies; generator fixedness makes all labels agree, and compactness plus intrinsic openness identifies the whole leaf. Projection preserves the essential meridian, contradicting its null positive displacement and proving contraction as required.

BLOCKED: F1 drops the supplier’s exact maximal-center-frontier contract. An attempt to unfold the search exposed an additional unmet cancellation hypothesis: its carrier requires a piecewise-C² separatrix frontier through the saddle, which generic C² data do not imply. For 0<α<1, u(x,y)=xy+|x|^(2+α) is C² with a nondegenerate saddle at zero, but its zero-level branch y=−sgn(x)|x|^(1+α) is C¹ and has unbounded second derivative. The frontier and scalar interfaces do not prove the needed boundary upgrade. No claim narrowing or unsupported repair was made.

Step 1.1 unnecessarily claimed nullness for every nearby positive displacement without citing its predicate. The repair only needs the one recurrent leaf B: if B were compact, its ambient image would be closed and would contain the limit x∈L, forcing B=L despite its positive collar points. Its strict return then makes its mutual-accessibility class open and distinct, and saturated closure gives the unchanged boundary conclusion.

The cap-bundle invocation omitted its nonspherical-universal-cover prerequisite. The repair adds the exact spherical-stability supplier as a direct dependency and applies its nonzero-Π consequence in the original leaf’s closed connected ambient component before constructing caps. All connected fences and subword reductions stay in that component, so every positive cap leaf meets the exclusion; the compact-boundary statement is unchanged.

The supposedly contradictory unrestricted interface is the companion counterexample’s Statement refuted, not an accepted theorem. The actual corollary requires closed M. The punctured-cylinder leaf has an essential small puncture circle bounding a hemisphere in the punctured ambient box, and no compact leaf capable of bounding a Reeb component. Venugopalan Theorem 1 supplies precisely the two dimension-five failures recorded here.
